paper/sections/03_rank.tex.old: The family theorem \cite[Thm.~1.2]{zywina} supplies the abstract rank and $2$-descent input; it does not itself assert that these displayed points form an integral basis.
paper/sections/03_rank.tex.new: An exact $2$-isogeny descent supplies the rank and $2$-descent input. Write $E'\colon y^2=x(x^2+45470x+91790289)$ for the $2$-isogenous curve, and $\alpha,\alpha'$ for the descent maps ($x$-coordinate modulo squares). Since $106272484=2^2\cdot4547\cdot5843$ and $22735^2-4\cdot106272484=3^2\cdot2243\cdot4547$, both descents are local at $\{2,3,2243,4547,5843,\infty\}$ and involve no class groups. The torsion points, $P_1$ and one point of $E'(\Q)$ give $\#\alpha(E(\Q))\cdot\#\alpha'(E'(\Q))=16=2^{r+2}$. This equals the Selmer bound, computed independently by PARI's unconditional \texttt{ellrank} and by eclib's \texttt{mwrank}. Hence $\rank E(\Q)=2$ and $\Sha[2]=0$, the $2$-Selmer rank being $3=2+\dim_{\F_2}E(\Q)[2]$. The family theorem \cite[Thm.~1.2]{zywina} gives the same conclusions for the whole family and is retained as corroboration. It does not itself assert that the displayed points form an integral basis.

paper/sections/03_rank.tex.old: The preprint qualification attaches to the imported family theorem; the basis computation has its own computer-assisted trust base.
paper/sections/03_rank.tex.new: No preprint input remains in this theorem. The descent and the basis computation each have their own computer-assisted trust base, and the descent certificate replays in seconds (\path{evidence/src/BSD_PERIMETER_Q36_2026-09-25/descent/}).

paper/sections/10_obstructions.tex.new: \item \emph{The prime-by-prime ladder} (\cid{X.14}). It was stopped at $13$. Climbing the ladder in order ($17$, $19$, $23$, \dots) moves only the conditional threshold ($2601\to3249\to4761\to\cdots$) and never reaches the infinite tail; a prime settled out of order does not move it, because the threshold advances only when the smallest remaining prime is excluded.
